title: “Dad brain”: How becoming a parent changes the brain, with Darby Saxbe, PhD

sentences.en: For many new parents, the first weeks and months after their baby is born are a time of deep bonding and bewildering changes.
sentences.zh: 对于许多新手父母来说，孩子出生后的最初几周和几个月，是建立深厚亲子关系和经历令人困惑的巨大变化的时期。

sentences.en: Between sleepless nights, scrambled schedules, and learning to meet the needs of a tiny infant, many new fathers and mothers feel like their world has been turned
sentences.zh: 在彻夜难眠、作息混乱以及学习如何满足婴儿需求的过程中，许多新手父母感觉自己的世界在一夜之间

sentences.en: upside down overnight.
sentences.zh: 天翻地覆。

sentences.en: Now it turns out those changes may go even deeper than parents realize.
sentences.zh: 现在看来，这些变化可能比父母们意识到的还要深远。

sentences.en: In recent years, scientists have found evidence that becoming a parent can change the structure and function of a person's brain.
sentences.zh: 近年来，科学家们发现证据表明，为人父母可以改变一个人的大脑结构和功能。

sentences.en: And crucially, these changes happen to fathers as well as to mothers.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，这些变化不仅发生在母亲身上，也发生在父亲身上。

sentences.en: So how does parenthood change us?
sentences.zh: 那么，为人父母是如何改变我们的呢？

sentences.en: What brain hormonal and other shifts occur in new moms and dads?
sentences.zh: 新手父母的大脑、荷尔蒙以及其他方面发生了怎样的转变？

sentences.en: Do these changes look different in men than in women?
sentences.zh: 这些变化在男性和女性身上表现得一样吗？

sentences.en: Or does becoming a father or a mother change the brain in the same way?
sentences.zh: 还是说，成为父亲或母亲对大脑的改变方式是相同的？

sentences.en: What advantages and risks might these changes confer?
sentences.zh: 这些变化可能带来哪些优势和风险？

sentences.en: And what does this research suggest about the best ways to support people through the transition to parenthood to benefit both parents and children?
sentences.zh: 这项研究对于如何最好地支持人们度过向为人父母的过渡期，从而造福父母和孩子，有什么启示？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Darby Saxby.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是达比·萨克斯比博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Saxby is an associate professor of psychology at the University of Southern California, where she leads the neuroendocrinology of social ties or NEST lab.
sentences.zh: 萨克斯比博士是南加州大学心理学副教授，她在那里领导着社会纽带神经内分泌学实验室（NEST实验室）。

sentences.en: She's interested in how close relationships affect health, particularly during major life changes, such as the transition to parenthood.
sentences.zh: 她关注亲密关系如何影响健康，特别是在重大人生转变期间，例如向为人父母的过渡。

sentences.en: She has studied brain changes in both fathers and mothers and how those changes are correlated with hormones and behavior.
sentences.zh: 她研究了父亲和母亲的大脑变化，以及这些变化如何与荷尔蒙和行为相关联。

sentences.en: Her research has been featured in media, including the New York Times, the Washington Post and NPR.
sentences.zh: 她的研究成果曾被《纽约时报》、《华盛顿邮报》和美国国家公共电台（NPR）等媒体报道。

sentences.en: And she's working on a book called Dad Brain, slated for release next year.
sentences.zh: 她目前正在撰写一本名为《父亲大脑》的书，预计明年出版。

sentences.en: Dr. Saxby, thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 萨克斯比博士，感谢您参加节目。

sentences.en: I'm very happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: I mentioned that you're working on this book, Dad Brain, and people might have heard the term mom brain or mommy brain before, maybe used in a pejorative way.
sentences.zh: 我提到您正在写《父亲大脑》这本书，人们可能以前听说过“母亲大脑”或“妈妈大脑”这个词，有时还带有贬义。

sentences.en: But what do you mean when you talk about dad brain or mom brain?
sentences.zh: 但当您谈论“父亲大脑”或“母亲大脑”时，您指的是什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what we're starting to discover, and there's this small but emerging neuroscience literature in humans, is that the brain is remodeled by parenthood.
sentences.zh: 我们开始发现——目前人类神经科学领域有少量但正在兴起的相关文献——大脑会因为人父母而重塑。

sentences.en: And we've known this for a while.
sentences.zh: 这一点我们已经知道一段时间了。

sentences.en: If you look at rodents, if you look at primates, that you see changes that are linked with adaptations that support nurturing a new infant.
sentences.zh: 如果你观察啮齿动物或灵长类动物，你会发现一些变化与支持抚育幼崽的适应性有关。

sentences.en: And it was really in 2016, there was a group in Spain that first looked longitudinally at moms who were recruited before becoming pregnant and then scanned for a second
sentences.zh: 直到2016年，西班牙的一个研究小组首次对母亲进行了纵向研究，她们在怀孕前被招募，并在婴儿出生几个月后进行了第二次扫描。

sentences.en: time a few months after the birth of an infant.
sentences.zh: 扫描结果听起来像个糟糕的笑话，但我们认为这实际上是件好事，那就是大脑变小了。

sentences.en: What they found is going to sound like a bad joke, but it's actually, we think, a good thing, which is the brain got smaller.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在受孕前和产后扫描之间，大脑损失了一些灰质体积。

sentences.en: So it lost some gray matter volume between that first preconception time point and the postpartum scan.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这可能是一个精简过程，有助于大脑在处理新手父母必须面对的所有社会信息时更高效地工作。

sentences.en: And we think that might be a process of streamlining and helping the brain work more efficiently when it comes to all the
sentences.zh: 这与儿童早期大脑因神经连接形成和修剪而损失体积的过程非常相似。

sentences.en: processing of social information that new parents have to do.
sentences.zh: 母亲大脑体积缩小的区域与心理化和社会认知有关。

sentences.en: So in much the same way that the brain actually loses volume in early childhood, as connections are formed and pruning occurs.
sentences.zh: 而那些体积缩小更多的母亲，随后报告说与婴儿的联系更紧密。

sentences.en: So areas in which the moms lost brain volume were those linked with mentalizing and social cognition.
sentences.zh: 就在这项研究发表的同时，我正在收集那些即将为人父母的父亲们的数据。

sentences.en: And moms who lost more volume subsequently reported stronger bonds with their infants.
sentences.zh: 我们在加州的实验室招募了期待第一个孩子的夫妇。

sentences.en: So I, at the same time that this study was coming out, was collecting data from dads who were transitioning to parenthood.
sentences.zh: 我们在孕中期对男性进行了扫描，然后在产后六个月左右又进行了一次。

sentences.en: So in our lab in California, we recruited couples who were expecting their first child.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的时间框架与西班牙的研究小组略有不同。

sentences.en: We scanned the men in mid-pregnancy and then again about six months postpartum.
sentences.zh: 但当我看到西班牙小组对他们追踪的女性的男性伴侣也有样本时，我立刻——好吧，不是立刻，花了几个月时间。

sentences.en: So our timeframe was a little bit different from the group in Spain.
sentences.zh: 我申请到了富布赖特奖学金。

sentences.en: But when I saw that the Spanish group had a sample of male partners of the women that they had followed, I immediately, well, not immediately, it took a few months.
sentences.zh: 我跳上飞机。

sentences.en: I got a Fulbright.
sentences.zh: 我去了西班牙，试图说服他们与我合作。

sentences.en: I hopped on a plane.
sentences.zh: 最终我们得以合并了样本。

sentences.en: I went to Spain and I tried to convince them to collaborate with me.
sentences.zh: 我们选取了我样本中的前20位父亲，以及他们扫描过的20位父亲，结果发现，在这两个样本中，男性表现出的变化与他们在母亲身上观察到的变化非常相似。当然也有一些差异。

sentences.en: And eventually we were able to pool our samples.
sentences.zh: 首先，这些变化更加细微。

sentences.en: So we took the first 20 dads from my sample, the 20 dads that they had scanned and found that across these two samples,
sentences.zh: 它们不那么显著。

sentences.en: we saw changes in the men that were actually really similar to the changes that they had already observed in the moMs. And there were a few differences.
sentences.zh: 它们不那么剧烈。

sentences.en: One was that the changes were more subtle.
sentences.zh: 对于母亲，你可以使用机器学习算法，仅根据大脑结构就能判断出她处于产前还是产后。

sentences.en: They were less striking.
sentences.zh: 而对于父亲，我们没有看到那么显著的效果。

sentences.en: They were less significant.
sentences.zh: 另一个区别是，在母亲身上，你看到了大脑皮层的变化，这是大脑表层，负责我们许多高级思维。

sentences.en: So with the moms, you can use a machine learning algorithm that will basically tell you whether a mom is pre or postpartum, just based on the brain structure.
sentences.zh: 还有皮层下结构，这更像是我们的“爬行动物脑”，包括杏仁核和一些情绪处理区域。

sentences.en: With the dads, we didn't see effects that were that striking.
sentences.zh: 而在父亲身上，我们只观察到大脑皮层的变化。

sentences.en: And the other difference was that in the moms, you saw changes to the cortex, which is sort of the top layer of brain tissue that does a lot of our higher order thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的重大发现。

sentences.en: And the subcortex, which is more kind of our lizard brain that includes the amygdala and some of our more sort of emotion processing regions.
sentences.zh: 随后，我在我的实验室中用更大样本的父亲数据复制了这一结果，并将这些变化与我们收集的育儿指标及其他指标联系了起来。

sentences.en: In the dads, we only saw changes to the cortex.
sentences.zh: 这种大脑体积的减少是会恢复，还是永久性的？

sentences.en: So that was our big finding.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题，我们目前还没有确切答案。

sentences.en: And then I've subsequently replicated that in my lab with a bigger sample of the dads that I've scanned and connected that with some parenting measures and
sentences.zh: 西班牙的研究小组确实在孩子出生七年后对一些母亲进行了扫描。

sentences.en: other measures that we've collected in our dads.
sentences.zh: 他们发现大脑体积的损失确实有所保留。

sentences.en: Does that brain volume come back or is this permanent?
sentences.zh: 虽然海马体等区域出现了反弹，但大脑整体仍然比怀孕前稍微小一点，或者我喜欢称之为“更精简、更敏锐”。

sentences.en: That is an excellent question that we don't really know the answer to.
sentences.zh: 不过我得说，因为七年后追踪这些人很困难，他们的样本量非常小。

sentences.en: So the Spanish group actually did scan some of the moms seven years after the birth of their child.
sentences.zh: 我想大概只有十几位母亲能够再次接受扫描。

sentences.en: And they found that there was some retention of the brain volume losses.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在正在对我们样本中的父亲进行扫描。

sentences.en: There was rebound in areas like the hippocampus, but the brain overall was still a little bit smaller, or I like to say like leaner and meaner, than it was before pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 我们正在进行七年后的随访。

sentences.en: So I should say though, that because it's hard to track people down after seven years, they had a really small sample.
sentences.zh: 希望当我们完成数据采集后，能够回答男性身上的一些相关问题。

sentences.en: I want to say it was like maybe a dozen moms that they were able to scan again.
sentences.zh: 这是在家庭中第一个孩子出生后的情况。

sentences.en: So we're now actually scanning the fathers in our sample.
sentences.zh: 如果有更多孩子，后续生育会发生什么，我们知道吗？

sentences.en: We're doing a seven-year follow-up.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And hopefully when we finish acquiring that data, we'll be able to answer some questions about that in men.
sentences.zh: 这也是个好问题，但我们还没有答案。

sentences.en: Now this is after the birth of the first child in a household.
sentences.zh: 我必须强调，这方面的文献非常少。

sentences.en: Do we know what happens with subsequent births if there are more kids?
sentences.zh: 它确实是一个新兴领域。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将在七年随访中关注这一点，因为我们的一些孩子确实有兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: Also a great question that we don't have the answer to.
sentences.zh: 我想现在有一半多一点的孩子有一个或两个兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: So I should emphasize this literature is really small.
sentences.zh: 丹佛大学的皮尔·永·金（Pil Yong Kim）做过一项研究，追踪了产后一到四个月的父亲。

sentences.en: It's really emerging.
sentences.zh: 所有的父亲都在出生后接受了扫描，但她在产后早期阶段进行了两次扫描。

sentences.en: So we will be looking at that with our seven-year follow-up because some of our kids do have siblings.
sentences.zh: 她的样本中既有初为人父的，也有二胎父亲，但样本太小，无法真正观察到群体差异。

sentences.en: I would say a little over half now have a sibling or two.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常好奇的一个问题是，父亲们是否会损失越来越多的体积？

sentences.en: There was one study done by Pil Yong Kim at the University of Denver that looked at fathers who were followed from one to four months postpartum.
sentences.zh: 大脑是否会变得越来越精简？

sentences.en: So all the dads were scanned after birth, but she scanned twice in that early postpartum period.
sentences.zh: 还是说在某个点之后，当你有了更多孩子，会有更多的反弹？

sentences.en: And she had a mix of first and second time dads, but the sample was too small to really look at group differences.
sentences.zh: 您还研究了男性成为父亲后可能发生的荷尔蒙变化。

sentences.en: So one of the questions that I would be really curious about is, you know, did dads sort of like lose more and more volume?
sentences.zh: 能跟我们详细说说这项研究吗？

sentences.en: Does the brain get more and more streamlined?
sentences.zh: 您发现了哪些变化，它们对日常生活有什么影响？

sentences.en: Or at a certain point, is there, you know, more rebound once you have more kids?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You've also looked at hormonal changes that can occur in men when they become fathers.
sentences.zh: 通常当我们想到荷尔蒙和为人父母时，我们会想到怀孕和分娩，对吧？我们知道这些是荷尔蒙非常丰富的事件。

sentences.en: Can you tell us more about that research?
sentences.zh: 但有大量证据表明，男性身上也会出现荷尔蒙变化。

sentences.en: I mean, what are some of the changes that you found and what are the everyday impacts?
sentences.zh: 研究最多的荷尔蒙之一是睾酮，我们知道它与力量、地位、支配地位和男性第二性征有关。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 它与男性紧密相关，尽管女性体内也有可检测到的睾酮水平，但男性的水平要高出许多倍。

sentences.en: So, so often when we think about hormones and parenthood, we think about pregnancy and birth, right, which we know are really hormonally rich events.
sentences.zh: 从观察啮齿动物和灵长类动物等双亲抚育动物的研究中，我们知道在后代出生前后，睾酮水平会下降。

sentences.en: But there's plenty of evidence that we see hormone changes in men as well.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们在人类身上也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: One of the biggest hormones that has been studied is testosterone, which we know of as a hormone that's linked with power, status, dominance, male secondary sex characteristics.
sentences.zh: 其中最令人印象深刻的研究之一是由圣母大学的李·格特勒（Lee Gettler）完成的。

sentences.en: It's very much associated with men, even though women also have detectable testosterone levels, but men's levels are many times higher.
sentences.zh: 这是一项来自菲律宾的大型研究，他们长期追踪了这些男性。

sentences.en: And we know from looking at biparental animals like rodents and primates that there are testosterone birth, testosterone drops around the birth of offspring.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有这些男性二十多岁时的睾酮测量数据。

sentences.en: And we actually see the same thing in humans.
sentences.zh: 多年后他们再次观察，发现与孩子同住的男性，尤其是花更多时间照顾孩子的男性，睾酮水平较低。

sentences.en: And so one of the most kind of impressive studies to look at this was done by Lee Gettler, who's at University of Notre
sentences.zh: 这项研究帮助回答了“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题，即：是睾酮水平较低的男性更容易成为父亲吗？

sentences.en: Dame.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始时就较低，并且保持较低，还是说有什么东西在改变？

sentences.en: This was a really big study from the Philippines and they followed men over time.
sentences.zh: 因为他们拥有这些纵向数据，他们能够说：实际上，成为父亲的男性在成为父亲之前睾酮水平更高。

sentences.en: They had testosterone measures from when the men were in their twenties.
sentences.zh: 然后他们表现出了更明显的下降。

sentences.en: And then they looked again years later and they found that men who were residing with children, especially men who were spending more time caring for children,
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来确实是一个随着时间推移而发生的变化，与成为父亲有关。

sentences.en: had lower testosterone.
sentences.zh: 我在我的实验室里也复制了这个结果。

sentences.en: And that study helped answer the chicken egg question of, you know, is it that lower testosterone men are selected into parenthood?
sentences.zh: 我们测量了父亲们的睾酮水平。

sentences.en: So they started lower and they stay lower, or is there something that's changing?
sentences.zh: 我们发现，较低的睾酮水平和睾酮的下降与参与婴儿护理的更高动力，以及在向为人父母过渡期间更好的关系质量有关。

sentences.en: Because they had this longitudinal data, they were able to say, actually, the men who became fathers had higher testosterone before they became dads.
sentences.zh: 所以这些荷尔蒙的变化确实带来了一些好处。

sentences.en: And then they showed more of a decline.
sentences.zh: 对于男性，我听到了这些好处。

sentences.en: So it really seems like there's a change over time that is linked with becoming a father.
sentences.zh: 那么女性呢？

sentences.en: And I've replicated that result in my lab.
sentences.zh: 她们的荷尔蒙如何变化？

sentences.en: We've measured testosterone in our dads.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we found that lower testosterone and a drop in testosterone are linked with more motivation
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们发现女性的荷尔蒙不仅会发生变化，而且还会对伴侣的变化做出反应。

sentences.en: to participate in baby care and better relationship quality across the transition to parenthood.
sentences.zh: 我们做了一项研究，观察了母亲和父亲的产后抑郁症。

sentences.en: So there were some benefits then to the changes in the hormones.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当父亲在孩子出生九个月后睾酮水平较低时，他们报告的抑郁感更多，但他们的伴侣在与睾酮水平较低的男性在一起时，实际上报告的抑郁感更少。

sentences.en: For men, I'm hearing what they are.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像“甲之蜜糖，乙之砒霜”的情况。

sentences.en: What about for women?
sentences.zh: 对于母亲来说，这种效应完全是由关系满意度来调节的。

sentences.en: How do their hormones change?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一位新手妈妈，你的伴侣的睾酮水平在孩子出生前后以一种适应性的方式下降，这可能会让你拥有更好的共同育儿关系，并免受抑郁困扰。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但对于男性来说，可能存在一些心理健康风险，我认为我们需要更多地了解这一点。

sentences.en: So actually, we found that not only do women's hormones change, but they're also responsive to the changes in their partners.
sentences.zh: 那篇论文的结论是，存在一个幸福的中间地带。

sentences.en: So we did a study where we looked at postpartum depression in both the mothers and the fathers.
sentences.zh: 男性在睾酮水平过高或过低时表现都较差，但有很多处于中间水平的男性，他们患抑郁症的风险似乎很低。

sentences.en: We found that when dads had lower testosterone about nine months after the
sentences.zh: 所以我不想让男性听了这些就认为，因为孩子出生前后睾酮下降，我的心理健康就会变得很糟糕。

sentences.en: birth of a child, they reported more depression, but their partners actually reported less depression when they were with lower testosterone men.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，这些荷尔蒙变化似乎是非常具有适应性的。

sentences.en: So there's a bit of a like good for the goose, not good for the gander kind of situation happening.
sentences.zh: 我还在想，有些男性听到这些可能会说，是的，但我的性欲会怎样呢？

sentences.en: And that effect for moms was totally mediated by relationship satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if you're a new mom, you have a partner whose testosterone is maybe dropping in an
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们知道向为人父母的过渡是对夫妻性生活的一次重大重组，对吧？

sentences.en: adaptive way around the birth of a child that might set you up to have sort of better co-parenting relationship and be buffered against depression.
sentences.zh: 因为通常在出生后的最初几个月里，会有禁止性行为的情况。

sentences.en: But there might be some mental health risks for men that, you know, I think we need to understand more.
sentences.zh: 而且，欲望也会发生变化。

sentences.en: The kind of takeaway from that paper though, was that there is a happy medium.
sentences.zh: 如果妈妈在母乳喂养，她可能不想被触碰，对吧？

sentences.en: Like men were doing worse at both very high and very low levels of testosterone, but there are a lot of men in the middle that seem to be a low risk for depression.
sentences.zh: 在夫妻关系方面确实发生了很多事情。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't want men to listen to this and think, you know, like I'm gonna, I'm gonna have terrible mental health because of testosterone drops around the birth of the baby.
sentences.zh: 所以，性欲的暂时下降可能并不是世界上最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: For the most part, it seems like these hormonal changes are really adaptive.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考进化论时，我们会考虑交配和育儿之间的权衡，对吧？

sentences.en: And I'm thinking also there are some men who may hear something like this and say, yeah, but what happens to my sex drive, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我们处于交配阶段，我们想要尽可能多地生孩子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们想要最大化我们的繁殖机会。

sentences.en: Well, and we know that the transition to parenthood is a big kind of reorganization of the couple sexual activity, right?
sentences.zh: 而如果我们处于更具抚育心态的阶段，我们想要照顾我们已经拥有的孩子，并确保他们能活到成年。

sentences.en: Because often there's prohibition against having sex in the first few months after birth.
sentences.zh: 随着社会变得越来越富裕和稳定，使用那种更具抚育性的策略实际上更具适应性。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's change in desire.
sentences.zh: 你不需要生一打孩子来祈求其中几个能活下来。

sentences.en: If the mom's breastfeeding, she may not want to be touched, right?
sentences.zh: 你实际上倾向于在仅有的几个孩子身上投入大量精力。

sentences.en: Like there's a lot that's going on kind of in terms of the couple relationship.
sentences.zh: 我们在工业化社会中看到了这一点，家庭规模变小了。

sentences.en: So, you know, a temporary drop in sex drive might not be the worst thing in the world.
sentences.zh: 这伴随着人们实施繁殖策略方式的转变。

sentences.en: And, you know, when we're thinking about evolutionary theory, we think about what is the trade-off between mating and parenting, right?
sentences.zh: 让我们花点时间谈谈睡眠作为这些变化的一个因素。

sentences.en: So if we're sort of in a mating place, we want to have as many babies as we possibly can.
sentences.zh: 为人父母的最初几个月通常涉及大量的睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: We want to maximize our opportunities to reproduce.
sentences.zh: 这会是导致这些大脑变化的另一个因素吗？

sentences.en: Whereas if we're more in a nurturing mindset, we want to take care of the babies that we do have and ensure that they live to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And as societies get richer and more stable, it's actually more adaptive to use that sort of more nurturing repertoire.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，每当我告诉任何人关于大脑、荷尔蒙或心理健康的这些工作时，他们总是说，嗯，对，这可能是因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: You don't need to have a dozen kids in hopes that a couple of them will survive.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: You actually tend to put a lot of investment into just a couple of kids.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: And we see that in industrialized societies, that family sizes get smaller.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: And that's kind of accompanied with a shift in how people enact their reproductive strategies.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about sleep as a factor in some of these changes.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: I mean, the first few months of parenthood generally involve a lot of sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: Could that be another factor in these brain changes?
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: And I think that's kind of the, anytime I tell anybody about any of this work with brain hormones or mental health, they always say, well, right, it's probably
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: because of sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 因为睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: And so we've measured sleep in our lab.
sentences.zh: 我们在实验室里测量了睡眠情况。

sentences.en: We found that when dads have more
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当父亲们大脑灰质体积

sentences.en: brain gray matter volume reduction, they also report worse sleep.
sentences.zh: 减少得更多时，他们报告的睡眠质量也更差。

sentences.en: But it seems like the sleep is actually not the cause, but the consequence of brain change.
sentences.zh: 但睡眠似乎并不是大脑变化的原因，而是其结果。

sentences.en: So we find that men who lose more gray matter volume across the transition to parenthood actually don't have worse sleep before
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些在向为人父母过渡期间大脑灰质体积减少更多的男性，在孩子出生前并没有更差的睡眠，

sentences.en: birth, but they have sort of increasingly worse sleep after birth.
sentences.zh: 但他们在孩子出生后，睡眠质量会变得越来越差。

sentences.en: So when you're sort of teasing out that direction of causality, it's a little bit hard to know what happens first, brain reorganization or sleep changes.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你试图理清这种因果关系时，很难判断究竟是先发生大脑重组，还是先发生睡眠变化。

sentences.en: Because when we're more motivated and engaged in parenting, we have worse sleep because we're getting up more often with the baby.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们更积极地投入育儿时，我们的睡眠会变差，因为我们需要更频繁地起床照顾孩子。

sentences.en: And therefore, our sleep is more disturbed.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的睡眠受到了更多干扰。

sentences.en: My understanding of the term mommy brain also refers to the fact that some women after giving birth start to feel like, I can't remember anything.
sentences.zh: 我对“妈妈脑”这个词的理解，也指一些女性在分娩后开始觉得：“我什么都记不住了。”

sentences.en: I don't know where I put my keys.
sentences.zh: 我不知道把钥匙放在哪儿了。

sentences.en: What am I doing today?
sentences.zh: 我今天要做什么？

sentences.en: It's the same thing happening to men under these circumstances.
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下，男性身上也发生了同样的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's actually this growing literature looking at cognitive changes with motherhood.
sentences.zh: 实际上，现在有越来越多的文献在研究母亲身份带来的认知变化。

sentences.en: And, you know, like you said, like mommy brain is often kind of disparaged as like this thing that makes you less smart.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你所说，“妈妈脑”通常被贬低为一种让你变笨的东西。

sentences.en: There's actually a lot of evidence that you sharpen your cognitive
sentences.zh: 但实际上有大量证据表明，你在成为母亲后，认知功能反而变得更敏锐了，

sentences.en: functioning after motherhood in the sense that you have more ability to remember and retrieve things that are specific to your infant, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你更有能力记住和提取与你孩子相关的信息，对吧？

sentences.en: So like, if you think about a rodent who has a whole bunch of babies running around, you can kind of forget where you put them.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你想到一只身边跑着一堆幼崽的啮齿动物，你可能会忘记把它们放在哪儿了。

sentences.en: And so like, there's a lot of stuff with like smell and the hippocampus that's linked with pup retrieval, like being able to find your pup, smell them and bring them back.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于嗅觉和海马体，有很多与幼崽找回相关的研究，比如能够找到你的幼崽、闻到它们并把它们带回来。

sentences.en: And in humans, you know, obviously we're not smelling our babies who, you know, have left the premises.
sentences.zh: 而在人类身上，显然我们不会去闻那些已经离开视线的孩子。

sentences.en: But we do need to remember a lot of different things when we're parenting in the early days and to be responsive to the specific stimulus of the babies.
sentences.zh: 但在早期的育儿过程中，我们确实需要记住很多不同的事情，并对孩子的特定刺激做出反应。

sentences.en: So it may be the case, not that we're becoming more forgetful, but actually just that we have more things to monitor.
sentences.zh: 所以情况可能并非是我们变得健忘了，而仅仅是因为我们需要监控的事情更多了。

sentences.en: And, and so there's a paper,
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，有一篇论文，

sentences.en: Jody Poluski, who's at the University of Rennes in France wrote that it says it's time to rebrand mommy brain.
sentences.zh: 法国雷恩大学的Jody Poluski写道，是时候为“妈妈脑”正名了。

sentences.en: We should actually think of it in a lot of ways as becoming more sharp and specific when it comes to certain things, you might have better retrieval of baby specific cues,
sentences.zh: 我们实际上应该在很多方面认为它变得更敏锐、更具体了，对于某些事情，你可能对婴儿特定的线索有更好的提取能力，

sentences.en: but worse retrieval of other things that aren't as important.
sentences.zh: 但对其他不那么重要的事情的提取能力会变差。

sentences.en: And my hunch is no one has really studied cognitive function in dads, but I think we would probably see something similar to the extent that you're engaging in caregiving.
sentences.zh: 我的直觉是，虽然还没有人真正研究过父亲的认知功能，但我认为，只要你参与了照料工作，我们可能会看到类似的情况。

sentences.en: You're tracking a lot of information relevant to your baby.
sentences.zh: 你正在追踪大量与你孩子相关的信息。

sentences.en: And so you might be losing your handle on some of the other things, you know, some of the other pieces of information that you're trying to keep track of.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会失去对其他一些事情的掌控，也就是你试图追踪的其他一些信息片段。

sentences.en: And I think the really interesting thing about all of this is that there's this increasing body of evidence that parenthood is neuroprotective in late life.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一切最有趣的地方在于，越来越多的证据表明，为人父母在晚年具有神经保护作用。

sentences.en: So work from the UK biobank and, um, and other sort of big data sources are linking number of children with markers of what we consider to be a younger looking brain.
sentences.zh: 来自英国生物样本库和其他一些大数据源的研究将子女数量与我们认为的“大脑年轻化”标志联系了起来。

sentences.en: So, and this is true in both men and in women, which tells us that it isn't just a pregnancy hormone thing.
sentences.zh: 这在男性和女性身上都适用，这告诉我们这不仅仅是怀孕荷尔蒙的问题。

sentences.en: It's like a caregiving experience thing that, um, the brain actually, if you use a, uh, sort of age adjusted
sentences.zh: 这更像是一种照料体验，如果使用一种年龄调整后的

sentences.en: algorithm to estimate how old the brain looks, it looks relatively younger among people that have had more kids.
sentences.zh: 算法来估计大脑看起来有多老，那么拥有更多孩子的人的大脑看起来相对更年轻。

sentences.en: So whatever's happening to the brain in early parenthood, it's hard to know whether it's good or bad, but it seems like, you know, at the end of the day, you get some benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论大脑在早期育儿阶段发生了什么，很难说它是好是坏，但归根结底，你似乎得到了一些好处。

sentences.en: How did you first become interested in this, uh, line of research?
sentences.zh: 你是如何开始对这个研究方向感兴趣的？

sentences.en: I've always been really fascinated with families and parenthood.
sentences.zh: 我一直对家庭和为人父母非常着迷。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think, um, my parents are divorced.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我的父母离婚了。

sentences.en: So I was always very interested in marriage and how couples figure things out because I, I sort of, you know, like, like any psychologist research is me search and
sentences.zh: 所以我一直对婚姻以及夫妻如何解决问题很感兴趣，因为我，就像任何心理学家一样，研究就是为了研究自己，

sentences.en: you want to understand that things that would fix your own life.
sentences.zh: 你想要理解那些能改善你自己生活的事情。

sentences.en: And so as a graduate student, I joined this lab at UCLA that was working with the data from the center for everyday lives of
sentences.zh: 所以作为一名研究生，我加入了加州大学洛杉矶分校的一个实验室，该实验室正在使用来自“家庭日常生活中心”的数据，

sentences.en: families, which was this big kind of psychology, anthropology, linguistics, archeology collaboration,
sentences.zh: 这是一个结合了心理学、人类学、语言学和考古学的大型合作项目，

sentences.en: where we basically went into families homes for a week and we followed them around.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上是在家庭中住了一周，跟踪观察他们。

sentences.en: We wrote down everything they did.
sentences.zh: 我们记下了他们所做的一切。

sentences.en: We took their stress hormones.
sentences.zh: 我们采集了他们的压力荷尔蒙。

sentences.en: Um, we asked them lots of questions and it was just this really interesting corpus of data kind of observing family life.
sentences.zh: 我们问了他们很多问题，这是一个非常有趣的家庭生活观察数据语料库。

sentences.en: And I was very interested in stress and parents and especially parents with kids, how they were managing the household.
sentences.zh: 我对压力和父母，特别是育有子女的父母如何管理家庭非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: But I thought if I'm going to have any hope of trying to make things better, I want to maybe go
sentences.zh: 但我认为，如果我想要有任何希望去改善现状，我可能想回到

sentences.en: back to the origin of when the family is first formed to try to understand, are there ways to prevent stress and adversity before they arise?
sentences.zh: 家庭最初形成的起源，试图了解是否有什么方法可以在压力和逆境出现之前就预防它们？

sentences.en: So that got me very specifically interested in transition to parenthood.
sentences.zh: 这让我对向为人父母的过渡产生了非常具体的兴趣。

sentences.en: And as kind of a couple's research, I was interested in that, like, how does a dyad become a triad and what does that do to the couple?
sentences.zh: 作为一名夫妻关系研究者，我对这一点很感兴趣：二人世界是如何变成三口之家的，这对夫妻意味着什么？

sentences.en: So I'm sort of like a backwards child development person in the sense that I start with the parents.
sentences.zh: 所以我算是一个“倒着看”的儿童发展研究者，因为我是从父母开始研究的。

sentences.en: We think of sort of developmental windows in infancy and early childhood, but I think there are also developmental windows when people become parents.
sentences.zh: 我们认为婴儿期和幼儿期有发展窗口，但我认为当人们成为父母时，也有发展窗口。

sentences.en: The brain's also changing.
sentences.zh: 大脑也在变化。

sentences.en: Hormones are also changing.
sentences.zh: 荷尔蒙也在变化。

sentences.en: Your social roles are also changing.
sentences.zh: 你的社会角色也在变化。

sentences.en: So I'm actually interested in the adult side of the equation because I think if you don't have good, healthy parents, you
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上对等式的成人那一端感兴趣，因为我认为如果你没有健康、良好的父母，

sentences.en: don't have good, healthy kids and then it affects the whole society.
sentences.zh: 你就不会有健康、良好的孩子，这会影响整个社会。

sentences.en: So I'm kind of going at it from the other side of the equation.
sentences.zh: 所以我正从等式的另一端着手研究。

sentences.en: How do the brain changes around parenthood compare with brain changes at other stages in life?
sentences.zh: 为人父母期间的大脑变化与人生其他阶段的大脑变化相比如何？

sentences.en: Does brain structure generally change throughout adulthood or are the changes that you see with the transition to parenthood very specific and unique?
sentences.zh: 大脑结构在整个成年期都会发生变化吗？还是说你在向为人父母过渡时看到的变化是非常具体和独特的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's hard to have great research designs to measure that because a lot of the studies out there are small and they don't always have control groups.
sentences.zh: 所以很难有很好的研究设计来衡量这一点，因为现有的很多研究规模都很小，而且并不总是有对照组。

sentences.en: So, you know, if we were to just track people in their early 30s for a couple years, would we see remodeling similar to what we're picking up on in parents?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们跟踪观察30岁出头的人几年，我们会看到类似于我们在父母身上发现的重塑吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so because it seems like we're seeing these consistent changes that aren't necessarily tied to chronological age.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为，因为我们看到的这些持续变化并不一定与生理年龄挂钩。

sentences.en: But the question of how dynamic is the brain structurally across the lifespan is one that we still need to understand better.
sentences.zh: 但大脑在整个生命周期中结构上有多动态，这个问题我们仍需更好地理解。

sentences.en: I will say like the Spanish group did a study where they compared brain changes in adolescence with brain changes across pregnancy and early postpartum and they found
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，西班牙的一个研究小组做了一项研究，比较了青春期的大脑变化与怀孕及产后早期的大脑变化，他们发现

sentences.en: that they were of similar magnitude.
sentences.zh: 它们在幅度上是相似的。

sentences.en: So we think of adolescence as this window of neural remodeling and it seems like the transition to parenthood is sort of a third window.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为青春期是一个神经重塑的窗口，而向为人父母的过渡似乎是第三个窗口。

sentences.en: Like if you think of early childhood as your first window, right?
sentences.zh: 就像如果你把幼儿期看作你的第一个窗口，对吧？

sentences.en: Like infancy, the brain is growing and remodeling.
sentences.zh: 比如婴儿期，大脑在生长和重塑。

sentences.en: Adolescence is your second window.
sentences.zh: 青春期是你的第二个窗口。

sentences.en: Transition to parenthood is your third window where there's kind of enhanced neuroplasticity and that would make evolutionary sense because we have this whole
sentences.zh: 向为人父母的过渡是你的第三个窗口，那里有增强的神经可塑性，这在进化上是有意义的，因为我们有一整套

sentences.en: repertoire of behaviors that we need to learn and we need to derive reward from in the same way that in adolescence, we need to individuate, we need to create peer relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们需要学习的行为库，并且需要从中获得回报，就像在青春期我们需要实现个性化、需要建立同伴关系一样。

sentences.en: There's a lot that we need to be able to do in adolescence.
sentences.zh: 在青春期我们需要做很多事情。

sentences.en: It's distinct from what our jobs were in childhood and I think that's true of the transition to parenthood.
sentences.zh: 这与我们在童年时期的任务不同，我认为向为人父母的过渡也是如此。

sentences.en: And then I think there's another window of remodeling around aging where you also see a lot of variability.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为在衰老过程中还有另一个重塑窗口，你也会看到很多变异性。

sentences.en: You see some adaptive changes.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一些适应性的变化。

sentences.en: We're just starting to figure out what is happening with the menopausal brain.
sentences.zh: 我们才刚刚开始弄清楚更年期大脑发生了什么。

sentences.en: Like women have been so understudied in our brain research.
sentences.zh: 女性在我们的脑科学研究中一直被严重忽视。

sentences.en: We don't know enough about brain health in women, but that's another time when you see changes in hormones.
sentences.zh: 我们对女性大脑健康的了解还不够，但那是另一个你会看到荷尔蒙变化的时期。

sentences.en: And so, you know, there's a lot of potential, I think, to better understand these windows of plasticity.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为在更好地理解这些可塑性窗口方面，有很多潜力。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下。

sentences.en: When we return, we'll talk about how paternity leave affects stress and mental health for fathers and mothers.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将讨论陪产假如何影响父亲和母亲的压力与心理健康。

sentences.en: Another area you've looked at is the impact of paternal leave, not just on dads, but on moms as well.
sentences.zh: 你研究的另一个领域是陪产假的影响，不仅是对父亲，对母亲也是如此。

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Let's talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: So we were lucky to be in California where we were collecting our data because not every state has this, but California does have a disability leave option for dads.
sentences.zh: 我们很幸运能在加州收集数据，因为并非每个州都有这种选择，但加州确实为父亲提供了残疾假选项。

sentences.en: So about half of the dads in our sample had some kind of access to paid paternity leave.
sentences.zh: 所以我们样本中大约一半的父亲有某种形式的带薪陪产假。

sentences.en: And when we looked at just a simple kind of group difference between dads who did and didn't have access to paid paternity leave,
sentences.zh: 当我们观察那些有和没有带薪陪产假的父亲之间的简单群体差异时，

sentences.en: we looked at prenatal to postpartum stress, mental health, and sleep.
sentences.zh: 我们观察了产前到产后的压力、心理健康和睡眠。

sentences.en: We found that dads had some benefit from the access to paid leave.
sentences.zh: 我们发现父亲们从带薪假中获得了一些好处。

sentences.en: Like they had, you know, better trajectories of sleep and stress, but it was really the moms that had the biggest benefit.
sentences.zh: 比如他们有更好的睡眠和压力轨迹，但真正获益最大的是母亲们。

sentences.en: So they had better trajectories of depression.
sentences.zh: 她们的抑郁轨迹更好。

sentences.en: They were less likely to develop postpartum depression.
sentences.zh: 她们患产后抑郁症的可能性更小。

sentences.en: They were less stressed and they had better sleep across the transition to parenthood.
sentences.zh: 她们压力更小，在向为人父母过渡期间睡眠质量也更好。

sentences.en: So I think of paternity leave as one of those things that really benefits not just dads, but the whole family.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为陪产假是那种不仅让父亲受益，而且让整个家庭受益的事情之一。

sentences.en: We know that it has benefits for kids.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它对孩子有好处。

sentences.en: We also know that it has benefits for the partner.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道它对伴侣有好处。

sentences.en: And I think anything as a stress researcher, it's like anything you can do to relieve stress on the family system.
sentences.zh: 作为一名压力研究者，我认为任何能减轻家庭系统压力的事情都是好的。

sentences.en: So any form of paid leave, whether to mom or to dad, I think can be really beneficial.
sentences.zh: 所以任何形式的带薪假，无论是给母亲还是父亲，我认为都非常有益。

sentences.en: And you certainly see that in other countries where there are sort of paternity leave incentives or take up programs that nudge more fathers into taking leave.
sentences.zh: 你在其他国家当然也能看到这一点，那里有各种陪产假激励措施或鼓励更多父亲休假的计划。

sentences.en: It sounds to me like there should be some public policy implications of this research.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这项研究应该有一些公共政策含义。

sentences.en: I mean, how do we go from, you know, the bench to reality?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们如何从实验室研究走向现实？

sentences.en: How do we apply this and get the changes that would let everybody benefit from what you're learning?
sentences.zh: 我们如何应用这些研究成果，并获得让每个人都能从你的发现中受益的改变？

sentences.en: This is what I think about all the time, right?
sentences.zh: 这是我一直在思考的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So if we think of this as a window of neuroplasticity, how do we reduce stress, which we know is bad for the brain?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们把这看作一个神经可塑性窗口，我们该如何减少压力，因为我们知道压力对大脑有害？

sentences.en: How do we allow space and time for healthy change, right?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何为健康的改变留出空间和时间，对吧？

sentences.en: Because if you think about, you know, every window of change is a window of vulnerability, but it's also a window of opportunity.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你考虑到，每一个改变的窗口都是一个脆弱的窗口，但它也是一个机会的窗口。

sentences.en: How do you maximize that opportunity?
sentences.zh: 你如何最大化那个机会？

sentences.en: So I think there's an interesting kind of two generation frameworks within research.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为研究中有一种有趣的“两代人”框架。

sentences.en: So you're looking at child outcomes, but you're also looking at parental mental health and parental psychological outcomes.
sentences.zh: 你不仅在关注儿童的成果，也在关注父母的心理健康和心理成果。

sentences.en: I think you can't really study kids without considering what's happening for parents.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果不考虑父母的情况，就无法真正研究孩子。

sentences.en: And there's so much concern now about this epidemic of youth anxiety and depression.
sentences.zh: 现在人们对青少年焦虑和抑郁的流行非常担忧。

sentences.en: But the fact is you look at parents of young people and they are also struggling.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，你看看年轻人的父母，他们也在挣扎。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, you, you sort of need to pay attention to the whole family system.
sentences.zh: 我认为你需要关注整个家庭系统。

sentences.en: So what's interesting right now is that there's all this kind of pro natalist talk.
sentences.zh: 所以现在有趣的是，到处都是这种“亲生育主义”的言论。

sentences.en: Like there was a New York Times article out yesterday to say yesterday saying the Trump
sentences.zh: 比如昨天《纽约时报》有一篇文章说特朗普

sentences.en: administration wants to get people to have more babies, but that isn't coupled with the kinds of policies that would motivate healthy baby having, right?
sentences.zh: 政府想要让人们多生孩子，但这并没有与那些能激励健康生育的政策相结合，对吧？

sentences.en: Like we're cutting head start at the same time.
sentences.zh: 比如我们同时在削减“启智计划”。

sentences.en: We're, you know, defunding Medicaid, which is where a lot of births happen.
sentences.zh: 我们在削减医疗补助，而很多分娩都是在那里发生的。

sentences.en: Why don't we have universal paid family leave for new parents?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们没有为新父母提供全民带薪家庭假？

sentences.en: Every other industrialized country has it.
sentences.zh: 其他所有工业化国家都有。

sentences.en: Even countries that are much wealthier, much less wealthy than us, have managed to figure out how to give generous a family leaves.
sentences.zh: 即使是比我们富裕得多或贫穷得多的国家，也已经设法弄清楚了如何提供慷慨的家庭假。

sentences.en: And there's a statistic that in the U S about a quarter of moms go back to work within two weeks of birth, which to me is just complete insanity.
sentences.zh: 有一个统计数据是，在美国，大约四分之一的母亲在分娩后两周内就回去工作了，这对我来说简直是完全疯狂。

sentences.en: Like what are we doing as a country if we can't allow parents the ability to bond with new kids?
sentences.zh: 如果我们不能让父母有能力与新出生的孩子建立联系，我们作为一个国家在做什么？

sentences.en: And I think it's like we have this very individualistic framework around parenthood.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对为人父母有一种非常个人主义的框架。

sentences.en: It's a choice.
sentences.zh: 这是一种选择。

sentences.en: If you decide to have kids, it's your job to take care of them.
sentences.zh: 如果你决定要孩子，照顾他们就是你的工作。

sentences.en: And I really need, think we need to step back and think about like kids are a public good.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为我们需要退后一步，思考一下孩子是公共产品。

sentences.en: We want healthy babies.
sentences.zh: 我们想要健康的婴儿。

sentences.en: We want healthy kids because that's our future workforce.
sentences.zh: 我们想要健康的孩子，因为那是我们未来的劳动力。

sentences.en: That's our national security.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的国家安全。

sentences.en: Those are the people that are going to be taking care of us when we're old, whether or not we ourselves choose to have kids.
sentences.zh: 无论我们自己是否选择要孩子，这些人都是我们老了以后会照顾我们的人。

sentences.en: We all benefit from having healthy, happy kids who are growing and thriving.
sentences.zh: 我们都受益于拥有健康、快乐、成长和茁壮的孩子。

sentences.en: And when we start to think of it as a public good, then I think we can unlock a little more political will for the kinds of policies that
sentences.zh: 当我们开始把它视为一种公共产品时，我认为我们就能为那些我们知道可以在过渡时期支持家庭的政策释放更多的政治意愿。

sentences.en: we know can support families during times of transition.
sentences.zh: 你最近在新闻文章中被引用，谈到了在研究中纳入多样化人群的重要性。

sentences.en: You were recently quoted in a news article about the importance of including diverse populations in research.
sentences.zh: 你是否研究过人们对早期为人父母的体验如何因种族、民族和社会经济地位而异？

sentences.en: Have you looked at how people's experience of early parenthood varies by race, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们知道在产后抑郁、压力和早期为人父母等结果中存在很多变异性，这些都与社会经济地位等因素有关。

sentences.en: So we know there's a lot of variability in outcomes like postpartum depression, um, stress, and early parenthood that are linked with things like socioeconomic status.
sentences.zh: 我们知道贫困确实是有害的，部分原因就是我们刚才谈到的家庭假问题。

sentences.en: We know that, um, poverty is really detrimental in part because of the family leave piece that we were talking about.
sentences.zh: 而且，在我的研究中，因为我们的样本量相当小，我们还无法深入挖掘群体差异。

sentences.en: And, um, in my studies, because we have pretty small samples, we haven't been able to dig too much into group differences.
sentences.zh: 我们已经尽力招募了我们能做到的最多样化和最具代表性的样本。

sentences.en: We've tried to recruit the most diverse and representative sample that we can.
sentences.zh: 但除了社会人口学差异之外，考虑文化也非常重要，

sentences.en: But in addition to sort of sociodemographic differences, it's also really important to consider
sentences.zh: 因为我们如何养育孩子以及我们如何对待育儿，很大程度上与我们自己是如何被抚养长大的有关。

sentences.en: culture because so much of how we parent and how we approach parenting is linked to how we ourselves were raised.
sentences.zh: 而且，拥有跨代同堂的家庭是规范吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, is it normative to have intergenerational households?
sentences.zh: 以不同的方式育儿是规范吗？

sentences.en: Is it normative to, you know, parent in a different way?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我倾向于认为我们所有人都是为了在社区中抚养孩子而设计的，而我们这种非常孤立的育儿模式正在让我们所有人都变得不快乐。

sentences.en: I mean, I sort of think that all of us were designed to raise kids in community and our very isolated model of parenthood is setting us all up to be unhappy,
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都是为了在社区中抚养孩子而设计的，而我们这种非常孤立的育儿模式正在让我们所有人都变得不快乐。

sentences.en: but you can see a lot of variability across cultures and how people approach that.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看到不同文化在对待这一问题的方式上存在很大的差异。

sentences.en: Now, we're mostly talking about new parenthood today, but I also want to ask you about an op-ed that you wrote recently.
sentences.zh: 我们今天主要讨论的是新手父母的话题，但我还想问问你最近写的一篇专栏文章。

sentences.en: It was published in the New York Times about under-parenting.
sentences.zh: 那篇文章发表在《纽约时报》上，主题是关于“低干预育儿”。

sentences.en: The idea that giving kids more space to be bored is good for both kids and parents.
sentences.zh: 核心观点是：给孩子留出更多无聊的空间，对孩子和父母都有好处。

sentences.en: What prompted you to write that op-ed and how does it tie in with your research on parenting?
sentences.zh: 是什么促使你写那篇专栏文章的？它与你的育儿研究有什么联系？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I'm a clinical psychologist, but I'm also an extremely lazy mom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是位临床心理学家，但同时也是个极其懒散的妈妈。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I wanted to write about this idea of giving kids downtime, giving them space to be bored, not letting them get over-occupied.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我想写写关于给孩子留出闲暇时间、给他们空间去感受无聊、不要让他们总是被各种事务填满的想法。

sentences.en: Because I think one of the things that is causing stress for parents and is actually dampening the birth rate is this sort of intensive style of parenthood
sentences.zh: 因为我认为，导致父母压力大、甚至实际上在抑制出生率的原因之一，就是这种高强度的育儿方式，

sentences.en: that has really just become prevalent in the last few decades.
sentences.zh: 这种方式在过去几十年里确实变得非常普遍。

sentences.en: So, Alison Gopnik has written about this, like the use of parenting as a verb is actually relatively recent.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·高普尼克（Alison Gopnik）写过相关内容，比如把“育儿”（parenting）当作动词来用，其实是相对较新的现象。

sentences.en: It's from the 1970s that we thought of parenting as like an activity that you do as opposed to just something that you are.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪70年代，我们才开始把育儿看作一种“你所做的事情”，而不是仅仅作为一种“你的身份”。

sentences.en: So, you know, we have this style that's very effortful.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们现在这种育儿方式非常费力。

sentences.en: It's always on.
sentences.zh: 它总是处于“开启”状态。

sentences.en: It's very child-centered.
sentences.zh: 它非常以孩子为中心。

sentences.en: We take kids to lots of activities.
sentences.zh: 我们带孩子参加各种活动。

sentences.en: We spend a lot of time shuttling them around.
sentences.zh: 我们花大量时间接送他们。

sentences.en: And it's very unusual kind of historically, if you think about the fact that in lots of cultures, kids aren't
sentences.zh: 从历史角度看，这非常罕见，如果你考虑到在许多文化中，孩子们并不

sentences.en: necessarily given lots of special activities to, you know, be escorted to.
sentences.zh: 一定会被安排参加各种需要专人护送的特殊活动。

sentences.en: It's more like they're following adults around.
sentences.zh: 更多的情况是他们跟着大人走。

sentences.en: They're modeling.
sentences.zh: 他们在模仿。

sentences.en: They're learning from what adults in the community do.
sentences.zh: 他们从社区成年人的行为中学习。

sentences.en: And they're contributing oftentimes very useful labor to the communities.
sentences.zh: 而且他们往往会为社区贡献非常有用的劳动。

sentences.en: So, we sort of have it backwards where I think we're rushing around trying to please our kids as opposed to our kids actually
sentences.zh: 所以，我们有点本末倒置了，我认为我们是在四处奔波试图取悦孩子，而不是让孩子

sentences.en: learning from us doing the things that we need to do as adults.
sentences.zh: 通过观察我们做成年人该做的事情来向我们学习。

sentences.en: And my interest in this, like I said,
sentences.zh: 我对这个话题感兴趣，就像我刚才说的，

sentences.en: I'm a very lazy mom, but it also just comes from studying parents and studying stress in parents
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常懒散的妈妈，但这同时也源于我对父母的研究、对父母压力的研究，

sentences.en: and thinking about, you know, how is it we've crafted this style of parenting and these expectations around parenting that feel pretty unsustainable, I think, for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 以及思考我们究竟是如何创造出这种育儿风格和围绕育儿的期望的，我认为这对很多人来说是相当不可持续的。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is if you look at the time diary trends from the 50s to today, we think of the 50s as like this
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，如果你看看从50年代到今天的“时间日记”趋势，我们会把50年代看作是

sentences.en: golden age of kind of like June cleaver, like doting motherhood, wearing an apron, you're always home.
sentences.zh: 那种琼·克莱弗（June Cleaver）式的黄金时代，比如慈爱的母亲，穿着围裙，总是待在家里。

sentences.en: Moms in the 50s actually spent less time per day than moms do now.
sentences.zh: 实际上，50年代的妈妈们每天花在孩子身上的时间比现在的妈妈们要少。

sentences.en: And what's interesting too is dads are also spending more time than they did in the 50s.
sentences.zh: 同样有趣的是，现在的爸爸们花在孩子身上的时间也比50年代多。

sentences.en: So, it's like the kid is just getting a lot more time with parents.
sentences.zh: 所以，孩子确实从父母那里得到了更多的时间。

sentences.en: Like we've just, you know, our model of parenthood is much more time intensive than it was a couple generations ago.
sentences.zh: 就像我们，你知道，我们的育儿模式比几代人之前要耗费多得多的时间。

sentences.en: You know, and I'm not even that old, but you know, when I was a kid in the 80s, I would just sort of like roam around my neighborhood and look for a neighbor to play with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我其实没那么老，但你知道，我在80年代还是个孩子的时候，我通常会在社区里转悠，找邻居一起玩。

sentences.en: And now, you know, the sort of modern style of parenthood is you organize a play date, you've set out snacks, you've got crafts ready to go.
sentences.zh: 而现在，你知道，现代的育儿方式是你要组织一场游戏约会，准备好零食，准备好手工活动。

sentences.en: It's all very curated, but it's not in the service of kids' ability to get unstructured play, which I would argue is kind of the central way that kids learn in childhood.
sentences.zh: 这一切都经过精心策划，但这并不利于孩子进行非结构化的游戏，而我认为这才是孩子童年学习的核心方式。

sentences.en: I'm with you.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: I'm a boomer and my mother would say, just get out of the house.
sentences.zh: 我是婴儿潮一代，我母亲会说，出去玩，别待在家里。

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎。

sentences.en: Just don't hurt yourself.
sentences.zh: 只要别把自己弄伤就行。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it was like if I was home for dinner, great.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我回家吃晚饭，那就很好。

sentences.en: Nobody worried.
sentences.zh: 没人会担心。

sentences.en: You know, I'm sure my parents had no idea where I was between the hours of 3 and 6 p.m.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我敢肯定，我父母根本不知道我每天下午放学后3点到6点之间在哪里。

sentences.en: every afternoon after school.
sentences.zh: 每一天都是如此。

sentences.en: So, what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么，你现在在忙些什么呢？

sentences.en: It sounds like there's still a lot of questions regarding dad brains.
sentences.zh: 听起来关于“父亲大脑”的研究似乎还有很多未解之谜。

sentences.en: Do you have more research underway at the moment?
sentences.zh: 你目前还有更多的研究正在进行吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: So, I mentioned we're doing our seven-year follow-up.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到的，我们正在进行七年后的随访。

sentences.en: So, we're bringing the families that we originally recruited in pregnancy back to the lab.
sentences.zh: 我们把最初在怀孕期间招募的家庭带回实验室。

sentences.en: So, the kids are six and seven years old now.
sentences.zh: 孩子们现在六七岁了。

sentences.en: The goal is to look at how prenatal stress and adaptation around the transition to parenthood affects child outcomes in middle childhood.
sentences.zh: 目标是观察产前压力和向为人父母过渡期间的适应情况，如何影响孩子在童年中期的成长结果。

sentences.en: And we're having the families do some interactive activities.
sentences.zh: 我们让这些家庭进行一些互动活动。

sentences.en: They're building a tower with blocks.
sentences.zh: 他们用积木搭塔。

sentences.en: They're doing an etch-a-sketch.
sentences.zh: 他们玩画板游戏。

sentences.en: We're looking at sort of joint play and attention.
sentences.zh: 我们正在观察他们的共同游戏和注意力情况。

sentences.en: And we're having the families engage in some discussions too about how the kid is faring and how the division of labor is going for the parents.
sentences.zh: 我们还让这些家庭讨论一下孩子的情况，以及父母双方的分工进展如何。

sentences.en: So, some of the same constructs that we were looking at in the first wave of the study.
sentences.zh: 所以，这和我们在研究第一阶段关注的一些结构是一样的。

sentences.en: So, we're about two-thirds of the way through collecting that data.
sentences.zh: 目前我们已经完成了大约三分之二的数据收集工作。

sentences.en: Hopefully, we'll be able to analyze it and have some results in the next five years or so.
sentences.zh: 希望我们能在未来五年左右分析完这些数据并得出一些结果。

sentences.en: And then, my other big thing is writing books.
sentences.zh: 另外，我的另一项大工程是写书。

sentences.en: So, I wrote the, I mean, it's not out yet.
sentences.zh: 我写了那本，我是说，还没出版。

sentences.en: It'll be out next spring, spring 2026, the dad brain book.
sentences.zh: 它将在明年春天，即2026年春天出版，是关于“父亲大脑”的书。

sentences.en: But I just turned in the manuscript a couple months ago.
sentences.zh: 但我几个月前刚交了稿子。

sentences.en: And I'll be working on that with my editor.
sentences.zh: 接下来我会和编辑一起处理后续工作。

sentences.en: And I was so fun to write.
sentences.zh: 写这本书的过程非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I just loved it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: It was such a delight to not have to write
sentences.zh: 不用写那些

sentences.en: statistics and research articles.
sentences.zh: 统计数据和研究论文，真是一件乐事。

sentences.en: Like, I love writing research papers.
sentences.zh: 虽然我喜欢写研究论文，

sentences.en: But it was so fun to just get to tell stories and not have to worry so much about, you know, going through the peer review gauntlet.
sentences.zh: 但能自由地讲述故事，而不必担心经历同行评审的重重考验，这真的太棒了。

sentences.en: And now, I'm writing my second book.
sentences.zh: 现在，我正在写我的第二本书。

sentences.en: And it's going to be about this underparenting concept and sort of how not to be a helicopter parent, how parents can relax and enjoy their kids more.
sentences.zh: 它将关于“低干预育儿”的概念，以及如何不做“直升机父母”，如何让父母放松下来，更多地享受与孩子在一起的时光。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: I'm hoping to dive into that soon too.
sentences.zh: 我希望很快也能投入到那本书的创作中。

sentences.zh: 好的，萨克斯比博士，非常感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
